title: Digital Pathology at Labcorp: AI, Whole-Slide Imaging & the Future of Diagnostics
summary: Discover how Labcorp is advancing digital pathology through whole-slide imaging, AI-enabled workflows, remote collaboration, and precision medicine to improve diagnostic efficiency, quality, and patient care.
body_markdown:
## Future of diagnostics through digital pathology?


Digital pathology is fundamentally transforming how pathologists work, how clinicians access diagnostic insight, and how patients receive timely, high-quality care. Across healthcare and life sciences, organizations are investing in digital pathology to improve collaboration, expand access to expertise, and support increasingly complex diagnostic workflows. As digital adoption accelerates, scalable infrastructure, image management capabilities, and evolving AI technologies are becoming essential components of modern pathology operations. Labcorp's ongoing investments in digital pathology reflect this broader shift toward more connected and data-enabled diagnostic workflows.


## What is digital pathology and why does it matter?


Digital pathology is the practice of converting traditional glass slides into high-resolution digital images - called whole-slide images (WSIs) - that can be viewed, shared, and analyzed on-screen rather than through a microscope. This shift unlocks capabilities that glass-based workflows simply cannot offer: remote access, simultaneous multi-slide review, AI-assisted analysis, and permanent, loss-proof digital archives.


For healthcare systems like Labcorp, digital pathology matters because it addresses core challenges facing modern diagnostics: growing specimen volumes, pathologist workforce shortages, geographic barriers to subspecialty expertise, and the increasing demand for faster, more precise diagnostic output.


**Building the infrastructure behind digital pathology adoption**


Successful digital pathology programs require more than slide scanners alone. Organizations must align imaging platforms, workflow tools, storage infrastructure, and review capabilities to support a range of use cases, from primary diagnosis and consultation to research and biomarker analysis. Labcorp's digital pathology strategy has evolved alongside these changing requirements, with investments designed to support multiple pathology workflows across the enterprise.


Labcorp has assembled a robust, enterprise-grade platform-agnostic digital pathology infrastructure designed for high-throughput clinical use. Key components include:


- **High-volume, FDA-cleared scanning platforms:** Labcorp has deployed more than 20 whole-slide scanners across global sites, including Philips’ Ultra-Fast Scanners (UFS), Roche’s DP600s, Leica’s GT450 DX, and Hologic Genius systems. These platforms enable digitization of slides for primary diagnosis, consultative review, immunohistochemistry, research applications, and GYN cytology interpretations
- **Robust image management and workflow platforms:** Across its diagnostics and clinical trial services, Labcorp uses leading image management systems, including Philips IntelliSite, Roche uPath, Proscia’s Concentriq for Research, and Hologic Genius™, to view digital slides, manage storage, support consults, and streamline review workflows
- **Cloud-enabled accessibility and remote reading:** Digitized slides can be accessed across Labcorp’s international network. This capability expands access to subspecialized pathologists while improving efficiency, turnaround times, and flexibility for distributed teams
- **AI-enabled workflow enhancement and decision support:** Labcorp is integrating advanced AI tools into its digital pathology ecosystem to assist with image analysis, biomarker interpretation, case prioritization, and quality review. These technologies help pathologists work more efficiently, improve consistency in diagnostic assessments, and support scalable, data-driven pathology workflows while keeping expert pathologists at the center of clinical decision-making.


## Role of digital pathology in improving patient care


The promise of digital pathology for patients is concrete and measurable. Labcorp is actively deploying digital and AI-enabled workflows across multiple areas of anatomic pathology to deliver better outcomes:


- **Faster diagnostic turnaround times:** Digital slides eliminate the logistical delays associated with physically transporting glass slides. Pathologists can review cases sooner and collaborate across distances more efficiently, reducing time to diagnosis
- **Enhanced quality, consistency, and safety:** Digital workflows minimize the risk of lost or damaged slides, allow simultaneous multi-slide review, consultation and comparison, and open opportunities for AI-enhanced decision support, improving diagnostic accuracy and reducing inter-observer variability
- **Expanded access to subspecialty expertise:** Through collaborations with internal teams and external partners such as Mount Sinai Health System and international pathology networks, Labcorp enables digital consults and second opinions without the logistical dependency on physically moving glass slides
- **Stronger support for precision medicine:** Digital pathology enhances the correlation between histology and genomic testing, enables algorithmic scoring of biomarkers such as PD-L1, and strengthens tumor content assessment-all of which are critical inputs for next-generation sequencing (NGS) workflows that inform personalized treatment decisions


## Pursuing AI and technology partnerships in digital pathology


Labcorp collaborates with leading technology innovators to bring the latest AI and imaging capabilities into clinical practice including:


- **Roche - Scanning Hardware for Primary Diagnosis:** Roche DP600 scanners deliver the speed, image fidelity, and regulatory clearance required for digital primary diagnosis and high-volume clinical use
- **PathAI - AI Algorithms and Enterprise Image Management:** Labcorp was an early strategic investor in PathAI, helping to support its growth as a commercially viable platform. Labcorp has recently licensed PathAI AISight as its enterprise image management system (IMS) to support scaled digital pathology for primary diagnosis. PathAI’s AI tools are particularly valuable for IHC prognostic marker interpretation and workflow efficiency
- **Hologic - AI-Enhanced Digital Cytology:** Digital cytology platforms such as the Genius™ Digital Diagnostics System support remote screening and[AI-assisted identification of atypical cervical cells](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/artificial-intelligence-cervical-cancer-screening-digital-cytology) , improving productivity and detection accuracy across cytopathology services


## Advancing drug development and biopharma research through digital pathology


Digital pathology is equally critical in accelerating pharmaceutical innovation. Labcorp’s Central Laboratory Services and Early Development teams have seen exponential growth in demand for whole-slide imaging, digital peer review, and advanced image analysis services.


Across global sites, Labcorp’s digital pathology capabilities support:


- Remote, GLP-compliant digital peer review
- High-volume scanning for exploratory endpoints and biomarker analysis
- Multiplex fluorescence imaging and advanced image analysis
- Streamlined global pathology workflows for complex clinical studies
- Real-world data generation from large-scale slide repositories


Labcorp’s platform-agnostic model spans diagnostics, central lab services, and early development to enable digital pathology support across the entire drug development lifecycle, aligned to the specific needs of biopharma customers.


## Supporting hospital and community pathologists with digital pathology


Many hospital and community pathology programs are evaluating digital technologies as they work to manage growing case volumes, staffing pressures, and increasing demands for diagnostic collaboration. Digital pathology can help support these efforts by improving access to images, reducing reliance on physical slide transport, and creating a foundation for future AI-enabled workflows.


Specific ways Labcorp supports hospital pathologist partners include:


- **Addressing turnaround time concerns:** When working with an off-site laboratory for slide preparation, digital delivery means that supporting pathologists are not limited by waiting for physical glass slides to arrive, accelerating workflows without compromising quality
- **Enabling image sharing across the care continuum:** Providing slides in digital form allows health systems to possess and share images for collaboration throughout a patient’s care journey, from initial diagnosis through treatment and follow-up
- **Introducing AI as a workload management tool** Digital pathology creates the medium through which AI tools can be applied to help pathologists manage growing workloads more effectively and efficiently, extending their capacity without sacrificing diagnostic rigor
- **Keeping pathologists at the center of patient care:** Rather than displacing pathologists, Labcorp’s approach is designed to advance their impact within their communities, keeping them at the interface between providers and patients while giving them better tools to do it


## How does digital pathology help address the pathologist's workforce shortage?


The healthcare industry faces[ongoing shortages](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/2026-pathology-staffing-cliff-why-digital-infrastructure-no-longer-optional) of pathologists and[histotechnologists](https://www.labcorp.com/education-events/articles/histotechnologist-shortage-digital-pathology) . Digital pathology is one of the most effective levers available for utilizing limited resources more efficiently. Labcorp is leveraging digital workflows to:


- **Enable remote reading** across sites and time zones, dramatically expanding the reach of each pathologist
- **Improve workload balance** by routing cases to available experts regardless of geography
- **Enhance training and education** through digital slide libraries that support resident and fellow development
- **Improve quality of life for pathologists** , including the ability to read from appropriate home offices or other locations and benefit from ergonomic improvements in the review process
- **Empower subspecialty support for rural and underserved communities** by virtually connecting subspecialist pathologists to patients in areas that lack local expertise
- **Optimize lab staffing** by locating laboratory facilities where there is a sufficient pool of histotechnologists to support the technical preparation of slides


By reducing dependency on physical glass slides, Labcorp is leveraging the availability of digitized slides to break down traditional geographic constraints, bringing pathologists virtually closer to the physicians and patients they serve.


## The future of pathology is increasingly digital


While adoption rates vary across healthcare settings, digital pathology is rapidly moving from an emerging capability to a foundational component of modern pathology practice. Advances in whole-slide imaging, cloud-based collaboration, AI-assisted analysis, and digital workflow management are creating new opportunities to improve efficiency, expand access to expertise, and generate deeper diagnostic insights.


Organizations across healthcare, research, and biopharma continue to evaluate how these capabilities can support their goals. Through ongoing investments in infrastructure, technology partnerships, and workflow innovation, Labcorp is working alongside the broader pathology community to help advance that digital future.
